# Generated file download chips

- New files under the runner's user-files root are discovered at turn end against a session baseline. The scan excludes hidden paths and dependency/cache directories, skips symlinks, and stops after 10,000 entries. Automatic publication requires the `artifact_publish` capability and passes through the existing pre/post tool policy hooks; denied or held publications do not upload bytes. Updates to existing paths are not automatically republished.
- Published files use the existing blob store and artifact ownership metadata. Canonical attachment blocks are appended to the first tool-role `event.turn-end`, which closes SSE and triggers the live history re-read. Workspace history renders those files outside the collapsible steps panel and recovers successful explicit publish results from older histories. Downloads use the authenticated, conversation-scoped `/api/files` endpoint.
- Artifact metadata IDs now hash the conversation ID and relative path instead of truncating the content hash. The old global content-derived primary key collided when identical bytes were published under different paths or conversations. Blob deduplication still uses the content hash; metadata upsert still uses conversation and path.
- Chat markdown removes artifact download links and `/api/files` links before rendering, leaving file chips as the download controls. The find pipeline uses the same transform so hidden download labels cannot count as matches. Ordinary links and code examples remain visible; workspace file previews retain their existing markdown behavior.
- Local preview uncovered a pre-existing stale-session failure: a Postgres session marked alive had no runner pod, so new messages queued into an unread inbox. Retiring that exact local session and clearing its conversation binding allowed a retry to spawn a fresh runner and finish. This PR does not implement runner/session reconciliation. Browser validation confirmed the poem chip downloaded before and after reload without a duplicate prose link.
